approval.cost: Free (the Bot Platform is described as free for users and developers)
approval.trigger: There is no review, approval, listing, marketplace, submission, or waitlist before real users can log in or message your bot: you create the bot and it works. An optional verification badge exists for official services ('for greater transparency'); it is a trust mark, not a gate, and is not required to operate.

blockers.detail: There are no scopes granting API access to a user's Telegram data (chats, contacts, files). Login proves identity only; all user data arrives inside the ID token, and Telegram provides no UserInfo endpoint. The only ongoing channel to the user is the bot conversation, plus bot-initiated direct messages if you hold the telegram:bot_access scope.
blockers.howToClear: Design honestly: use Telegram login for identity and the Bot API as the product surface. If your product needs delegated access to user data, Telegram cannot provide it.
blockers.title: Identity-only: no delegated access to user data exists

blockers.detail: In @BotFather's Login Widget section you register every origin where the login widget is embedded and every OIDC redirect URI. 'For security reasons, Telegram will only process logins or redirect users using your pre-registered URLs.' An unregistered origin simply fails.
blockers.howToClear: Register production, staging, and local origins up front; revisit whenever URLs change.
blockers.title: Allowed URLs are a hard gate

blockers.detail: The bot token is the Bot API master credential ('everyone who has your token will have full control over your bot'), the legacy login verification keys derive from it, and the OIDC client secret comes from the same BotFather surface. There is no scoped sub-credential to fall back on.
blockers.howToClear: Vault bot credentials like root keys, and plan a token-reset procedure before you need one.
blockers.title: One credential, total compromise

alternatives: Legacy Login Widget (JS iframe): /setdomain links one domain; the widget returns id, name, username, photo_url, auth_date, hash, verified server-side with HMAC-SHA-256 keyed by SHA256(bot token). Documented but explicitly legacy

flavor.recommended: A bot created via @BotFather, which doubles as the OIDC client for 'Log In With Telegram'; the bot itself (Bot API) is the product surface inside Telegram
flavor.why: Telegram has no developer portal and no app registry; the bot is the anchor object for everything. Its login is genuine standards-based OIDC (discovery at oauth.telegram.org, Authorization Code with PKCE), but it is identity-only: scopes are openid (required), profile, phone, and telegram:bot_access (permission for your bot to message the user). No delegated data-access grant exists, for anyone.

humanMust: Create the bot by messaging @BotFather inside Telegram (no web portal exists)
Register Allowed URLs and retrieve the Client ID/Secret in BotFather's Login Widget section
Users tap to confirm login in Telegram
name: Telegram
nuances: Bots can't start conversations with users; a user must add the bot to a group or message it first. In groups, Privacy Mode means bots only see relevant messages by default, and bot cloud storage is limited (older messages may be removed).
No documented refresh token: the token response is an access token (documented expires_in 3600) plus the ID token, and that is all.
Front-end gotcha: the JS login library uses a popup; a Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin header blocks the cross-window communication and login fails (use same-origin-allow-popups).
Choosing EdDSA or ES256K signing (Web3 use) restricts you to the openid scope; profile and phone requests will reject with those algorithms.
Telegram describes the platform as hosting more than 10 million bots; discoverability, not approval, is your distribution problem.
prerequisites: A bot (created via @BotFather) and custody of its token
Your login origins and redirect URIs, registered as Allowed URLs

steps.detail: Message @BotFather on Telegram, register a bot, and receive its bot token (the master credential). Telegram recommends matching the bot's name and profile picture to your site, since users see them in the login confirmation.
steps.title: Create the bot via @BotFather

steps.detail: In the @BotFather mini app: select the bot > Login Widget > add every origin where the login widget is embedded and every OIDC redirect URI. The same screen shows the bot's Client ID (its bot ID) and Client Secret; store them securely.
steps.title: Register Allowed URLs; note the Client ID and Secret

steps.detail: Embed the Telegram Login JS library (or native iOS/Android SDKs), or configure any standard OIDC library (Keycloak, Auth0, etc.) with the discovery document at oauth.telegram.org/.well-known/openid-configuration, your Client ID/Secret, response_type=code, and PKCE (S256 recommended). Request openid plus profile, phone, or telegram:bot_access as needed; a nonce is supported.
steps.title: Integrate the OIDC client

steps.detail: POST the code to oauth.telegram.org/token with Basic auth (base64 client_id:client_secret) and the PKCE verifier. The response carries an access token and an ID token; ALL user data is in the ID token (there is no UserInfo endpoint; configure libraries to skip userinfo). Validate the ID token against the JWKS (signature, iss = oauth.telegram.org, aud = your bot ID, exp); RS256 is the default signing algorithm.
steps.title: Exchange the code and validate the ID token

steps.detail: Only if supporting the old widget: send /setdomain to @BotFather, embed the widget script with your bot's username, and on every login verify the returned hash server-side (HMAC-SHA-256 over the data-check-string, keyed by SHA256(bot token)) plus auth_date freshness.
steps.title: (Legacy path) Verify widget logins with HMAC

tagline: No portal, no registry, no review: the 'app' is a bot from @BotFather. Its login is real OIDC, but identity-only; there are no scopes into a user's Telegram data, and the bot conversation is the actual product surface.

time.active: ~10 min in BotFather + ~1-2 hrs of standard OIDC integration
time.total: Same day; the platform is self-serve end to end
